analysis:
The PR makes one security-relevant change in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml. It adds a job-level env DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod to the qualify-sdk job (head lines 239-242) and edits a comment at head lines 180-182. The build-provider job (head line 183) still compiles with the resolved environment, so the shipped artifact's environment identity is unchanged. The change affects only the qualification lane: tests now run against production defaults on every branch, including dev, where Package.swift would otherwise default to the dev identity. That makes qualification stricter and more consistent with ci.yml; it does not weaken it.

I saw no new secrets, permissions, triggers, or credential exposure. qualify-sdk keeps contents: read, and the signing and publication jobs are untouched. Their source-verification gate, exact-artifact digest download, and per-environment secret scoping are unchanged. The base-side unit covers the publish-release and validate-older-macos jobs, which the PR does not modify.

Relevant threat IDs are T-034, T-054, and A-017 (build qualification and provenance). The remaining question is outside the supplied evidence: whether the provider-release-build action's lane=qualification logic reads DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT or the environment input consistently. That action was not supplied. I flag it only as an unverified contract, not as a regression. The affected code is not part of the TB-007 prefix-cache path or T-041.
